issues.failure_explanation: The theorem claims a unique viscosity solution in C^{0,1}_b and defines Z^lambda pointwise through the gradient of that viscosity solution. Under Assumption \ref{assumptions} the terminal data g is only Lipschitz (possibly unbounded) and the barriers in Assumption \ref{assumption2} are only C^{1,2} off hypersurfaces, so V^lambda need not be bounded (ruling out the class C^{0,1}_b, e.g. g(x)=x is admissible and makes V^lambda unbounded), and a viscosity solution carries no pointwise gradient; the formula Z^lambda_t = sigma(t,X_t) nabla_x V^lambda(t,X_t) is therefore not even well defined as stated. The cited results support at most the Markovian identification Y^lambda_t = V^lambda(t,X_t) in the viscosity sense.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the theorem as: the PDE has a unique viscosity solution in the usual class of continuous functions of linear growth, Y^lambda_t = V^lambda(t,X_t), and Z^lambda coincides with sigma nabla V^lambda only dP x dt-a.e. under additional regularity (or delete the Z-formula); this preserves every use of the theorem.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thmpde as stated is not established: the claimed bounded-Lipschitz class can fail to contain the solution and the pointwise Z-representation is ill-defined. Downstream results use only Y^lambda_t = V^lambda(t,X_t) (Corollary stoapb, Theorem ydiffbound), which remains valid by standard viscosity Feynman–Kac arguments, so no labelled downstream result is invalidated.
issues.title: Theorem thmpde asserts a pointwise gradient representation and C_b^{0,1} regularity that are not available for a viscosity solution
issues.why_classification: A contained restatement (standard viscosity identification plus an a.e. gradient clause, or an added regularity hypothesis) preserves the theorem and every downstream use; no new architecture is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
There exists a constant $\kappa>0$ such that, for all $(t,x)\in[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d$ and all $\xi\in\mathbb{R}^d$,
        \[
        \xi^\top \big(\sigma(t,x)\sigma(t,x)^\top\big)\,\xi \;\ge\; \kappa\,|\xi|^2.
        \]

issues.failure_explanation: The example claims the model satisfies Assumption \ref{assumptions} and \ref{assumptionpde}, both of which require uniform ellipticity on all of [0,T]xR^d. For the stated model sigma(s,x) = sigma diag(x^1,...,x^d), so sigma sigma^T = sigma^2 diag((x^i)^2), which is singular: taking xi = e_1 and x with x_1 = 0 gives xi^T sigma sigma^T xi = 0 < kappa xi^2 for any kappa > 0. Hence the claimed verification is false; the degeneracy at x = 0 (and coordinatewise) is intrinsic to geometric Brownian motion.

failure_location.quote: Then, it is straightforward to check that Assumptions~\ref{assumptions} and \ref{assumptionpde} hold.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reformulate the example under a log-transform (where diffusion coefficients are bounded and uniformly elliptic), or weaken Assumptions to uniform ellipticity/nondegeneracy holding along the support of X together with local versions of the PDE identification, and re-verify Assumption \ref{assumption2} in the transformed variables.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's flagship financial example is not covered by the stated framework: Theorems thm:added-1, thm:added-2, thmpde, Proposition apb1 and the subsequent error analysis all require uniform ellipticity on the whole domain, which the example violates.
issues.title: Black–Scholes example does not satisfy the uniform ellipticity assumption it claims
issues.why_classification: The repair requires reformulating the framework's ellipticity hypothesis and re-verifying the example's obstacle geometry (contained but nontrivial); the paper's conclusions themselves need not be abandoned.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since \(x_0\notin\Gamma\), the function \(p_b\) is \(C^{1,2}\) in a neighborhood of \((t_0,x_0)\).

issues.failure_explanation: At (t0,x0) the test phi touches V^lambda from below (V^lambda - phi has a local minimum 0), so the viscosity supersolution inequality for the equation \mathcal{L}u + f_\lambda = 0 is \mathcal{L}\phi + f_\lambda(\phi) \le 0, i.e. -\mathcal{L}\phi - f_\lambda \ge 0, which is exactly the sign used later in the paper (equation T5:1 of Theorem ydiffbound). Proposition apb1's proof instead asserts \mathcal{L}\phi + f_\lambda \ge 0 at such a lower touch, which is the subsolution-side inequality and is false in general (e.g. the classical solution u = x of \partial_t u + \frac12 u_{xx} = 0 with a lower test u - \varepsilon x^2 gives \mathcal{L}\phi = -\varepsilon < 0). With the correct sign, the subsequent chain (eq:prop1) must be reversed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the viscosity inequality at the lower touch by \mathcal{L}\phi + f_\lambda(\phi) \le 0 (and correspondingly for \phi_\eta in Case 2 and for the p_w mirror), and reverse the directions of the inequalities in the chain (eq:prop1) and its Case-2 analogue; the stated bounds of Proposition apb1 then follow verbatim (as the sharper (lambda-K_y) sup <= -D_b <= D_b^-).
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Proposition apb1 as written is invalid (it uses the subsolution-side inequality at a minimum point). The stated bounds are nevertheless recoverable: with the correct inequality the same substitutions yield (lambda - K_y) sup_K ell <= -D_b, which implies the claimed (lambda-K_y)(V^lambda - p_b)^- <= D_b^- a fortiori, and the mirror argument for p_w likewise survives.
issues.title: Wrong-signed viscosity inequality in the proof of Proposition apb1
issues.why_classification: The repair is a mechanical sign flip along an already-written computation; the substantive conclusion (the barrier-defect bounds) is unchanged, indeed strengthened.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For $X_0\in L^2(\Omega)$, we study BSDEs of the form

Suppose Assumptions \ref{assumptions}, \ref{assumptionpde}, and \ref{assumption2} hold. ... Then, we have    $$\|Y^\lambda\|^p_{\mathbb{S}^p}+\|Z^\lambda\|^p_{\mathbb{H}^p}\le C_2$$
    for any $p\ge2$.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed estimates \|X\|_{S^p}^p < C_2, \mathbb{E}|X^{\tilde\pi}_{t_i}|^p \le C_2 and the strong Euler error bound are asserted 'for any p >= 2', but the only integrability hypothesis on the initial condition is X_0 \in L^2. If X_0 has a finite second but infinite p-th moment (which Assumption \ref{assumptions} permits), then E sup_t |X_t|^p = \infty and all three claims are false for p > 2; Proposition xyzbound, whose proof invokes (xbound) for arbitrary p, inherits the gap for p > 2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that X_0 \in L^p for every p >= 2 (standard and harmless in the intended applications), or restate the estimates and Proposition xyzbound for p = 2 only.
issues.overall_effect: The 'for any p >= 2' scope of the three displayed estimates and of Proposition xyzbound is unsupported; all conclusions survive if the estimates are restricted to p = 2 (the only case used downstream) or if X_0 \in L^p for all p is assumed.
issues.title: Euler/moment estimates are claimed for all p>=2 but X_0 is only in L^2
issues.why_classification: A standard local strengthening of the hypothesis (or restriction to p = 2) restores every statement and all downstream uses; no rate, construction, or conclusion changes.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof needs \int_t^{\tau_{i+1}} \mathbb{E}|Z^\lambda_s|^p ds \le \frac1N \mathbb{E}\big[(\int_t^{\tau_{i+1}}|Z^\lambda_s|^2ds)^{p/2}\big] to absorb the Z-term. This holds only for p = 2 (where the two sides are equal); for p > 2 it is false in general: for a deterministic Z_s \equiv c the left side equals (\tau_{i+1}-t)c^p while the right side equals (1/N)(\tau_{i+1}-t)^{p/2}c^p, and (\tau_{i+1}-t)^{1-p/2} \ge 1 makes the claimed bound fail. Since the subsequent absorption step ('Choosing N > 2C_2') relies on this estimate, the L^p bound on Z^lambda is not established by the written argument for p > 2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the step by the standard estimate E(\int_t^\tau |Z_s|^2 ds)^{p/2} \ge (\tau-t)^{p/2}\sup_s \mathbb{E}|Z_s|^p-type absorption, or first derive the H^2 bound and then obtain the H^p norm via the usual BGI/energy-identity argument with a constant depending on p; this is the standard contained fix and the stated proposition remains true.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Proposition xyzbound is incomplete for p > 2; the p = 2 case (the only one invoked later, in Corollary apbcor and Theorems discerror, penaltyerror, better) is recoverable, so no downstream labelled result loses validity.
issues.title: False moment estimate in the proof of Proposition xyzbound
issues.why_classification: A routine, local reorganisation of a standard a priori estimate restores the proof; the statement and all its uses remain intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
so that the balancing choice
$\lambda\asymp \Delta t^{-1/2}$ yields the rate $O(\Delta t^{1/4})$ for the value process.

issues.failure_explanation: The proven bound is sqrt(max E|Y - Y^lambda|^2) <= C_2(lambda Delta t^{1/2} + 1/lambda). With the claimed choice lambda = Delta t^{-1/2} the right-hand side equals C_2(1 + Delta t^{1/2}), which does not even vanish; the paper's own bound therefore contradicts the claimed O(Delta t^{1/4}) rate. The bound is balanced (minimised) at lambda = Delta t^{-1/4}, giving Delta t^{1/4}. The same wrong tuning appears in the Contributions: 'the balancing choice \lambda\asymp \Delta t^{-1/2} yields the rate O(\Delta t^{1/4})'.
